claim.pdf_says: Page 1021 (printed 991) ends with "Buginese:\n1A17-1A1B". "Buhid:" is the FIRST line printed on page 1022 (printed 992), directly above "1752-1753".
claim.markdown_says: End of the page-1021 block: "Buginese:\n1A17-1A1B Buhid:". The page-1022 block then opens with a headless "1752-1753".
claim.why_it_matters: Annex B list 2) "characters permitted in a user-defined word except as the start character" is normative. The label Buhid is separated from its range 1752-1753 across the page break, so the entry cannot be read or extracted correctly from the markdown.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed on both sides of the page break at 300 dpi. PDF p1021 (printed 991): the bottom crop shows the last body lines are 'Brahmi:' / '11000-11002, 11038-11046, 11066-1106F, 1107F', then 'Buginese:' / '1A17-1A1B', then ~1.5 inches of white space, then the footer '(C)ISO/IEC 2023   991'. There is no 'Buhid:' glyph anywhere on page 1021. PDF p1022 (printed 992): the top crop shows the running head 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)', then the first body entry 'Buhid:' / '1752-1753', then 'Chakma:'. Markdown specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 40772 (page-1021 block) reads '1A17-1A1B Buhid:' as its final line; the page-1022 block opens with the anchor, '## Page 1022', '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)', then a bare '1752-1753' with no label above it. So the transcription pulled page 1022's first label backward onto page 1021 and concatenated it onto Buginese's range line. This is not mere page-break furniture, line wrapping or hyphenation: no reflow of a wrapped line is involved (Buginese's range is a single short line that does not wrap, and the PDF puts a blank line plus a page boundary plus a running head between '1A17-1A1B' and 'Buhid:'). The defect changes what the text asserts on a plain reading: 'Buginese:\n1A17-1A1B Buhid:' reads as the Buginese entry carrying a trailing dangling token, and '1752-1753' is left unattributed, so a reader or extractor of the normative XID_Continue repertoire either drops 1752-1753 or misattributes it to the preceding script. Rejection tests all fail: the text is not merely reflowed onto an adjacent line (it crosses a page block boundary and joins a different entry), the claim quotes both sources correctly, and the association Buhid->1752-1753 is genuinely broken. NOT a one-off: the identical page-break orphan occurs 19 times in the two Annex B repertoire lists. Verified sibling on the very next page - markdown page-1022 block ends '0AFA-0AFF Gunjala_Gondi:' while the PDF p1022 bottom crop ends at 'Gujarati:' / '0A81-0A83, ... 0AE6-0AEF,' / '0AFA-0AFF' with no 'Gunjala_Gondi:' on the page. Full list of affected page blocks and lines in specs/ISO_COBOL.md: p1010 L40182 '1E900-1E943, 1E94B Ahom:'; p1011 L40235 '1A00-1A16 Buhid:'; p1014 L40403 'A984-A9B2 Kaithi:'; p1015 L40454 '10600-10736, 10740-10755, 10760-10767 Linear_B:'; p1016 L40506 '10980-1099F Miao:'; p1017 L40558 '10C80-10CB2, 10CC0-10CF2 Old_Italic:'; p1018 L40610 '10B80-10B91 Rejang:'; p1021 L40772 '1A17-1A1B Buhid:'; p1022 L40824 '0AFA-0AFF Gunjala_Gondi:'; p1023 L40876 '17B4-17D3, 17DD, 17E0-17E9 Khojki:'; p1024 L40928 '11630-11640, 11650-11659 Mongolian:'; p1025 L40981 'A880-A881, A8B4-A8C5, A8D0-A8D9 Sharada:'; p1213 L49030 '312D-312F, 31B8-31BF Brahmi:'; p1214 L49087 '...FE2E-FE2F Deseret:'; p1216 L49207 '11080-110BA Kannada:'; p1217 L49263 '10280-1029C Lydian:'; p1218 L49319 '16A40-16A5E, 16A60-16A69 Multani:'; p1219 L49374 '10A60-10A7C Old_Turkic:'; p1220 L49431 '...1DAA1-1DAAF Sinhala:'.
verdict.corrected_description: CONFIRMED, with one correction of scope and one of emphasis. Correction of emphasis: no text is lost - the token 'Buhid:' IS present in the markdown, but it is attached to the wrong page block and glued onto the end of the preceding script's range line, which orphans both the label (now reading as trailing noise after Buginese's range) and the range 1752-1753 (now headless at the top of the page-1022 block). Correction of scope: this is not a page-1021 incident but a systematic transcription defect affecting 19 script entries across both Annex B repertoire lists - list 1) start characters (page blocks 1010, 1011, 1014-1018) and list 2) non-start characters (page blocks 1021-1025), plus the corresponding lists at page blocks 1213-1220. In every case the first script label printed at the top of page N+1 was pulled back and appended to the last range line of page N. Exact page-1021 facts: PDF p1021 (printed 991) ends 'Buginese:' / '1A17-1A1B' followed only by white space and the footer; PDF p1022 (printed 992) opens with the running head then 'Buhid:' / '1752-1753'. Fix: for each of the 19 listed lines, split the trailing '<Script>:' label off the range line and move it to the head of the following page block, immediately above its range line.
